subject: physical-education
essentialQuestion: How can understanding lifetime activity portfolio help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?

prompts.prompt: Explain activity preferences in your own words and give or identify a valid example.
Use a diagram, model, quotation, data display, map, demonstration, or worked process to show understanding of community resources.
Apply stress and enjoyment in a new realistic situation. Show the process or cite evidence.
Analyze a plausible error, weak claim, unsafe choice, or design flaw involving independent planning; correct it and explain why.
Connect activity preferences with long-term participation. Explain how the ideas support, constrain, contrast with, or build on one another.
Present the strongest evidence from the unit project: Present a lifetime-activity portfolio and a realistic next-season plan.
Identify one skill you can now transfer, one check that improves accuracy or quality, and one next question.

adaptationChoices: Access supports may change format, pacing, quantity, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
